---
title: "Hackathon 3"
subtitle: "Exploring LLMs for research and FAIR data"
---

This hackathon will be held on 27 November at the [SURF](https://www.surf.nl/en) in Amsterdam. It will **bring together** researchers, developers, data managers and infrastructure experts to **explore practical uses of large language model (LLMs)**.

The morning presentations will set the stage by **introducing key topics** such as LLM services and developments at SURF Research Cloud, AI for analysis-ready data, as well as LLM-based metadata extraction, data access brokers, and data discovery. Participants will **briefly pitch their challenges, experiences or project** related to LLMs.

The afternoon is dedicated to a hackathon that is deliberately designed to be **flexible and participant-driven**. It will be shaped around the participants by considering their backgrounds, interests and projects. They will **form groups around shared goals and complementary expertise**, and use the afternoon to work hands-on on their own use cases, data, software, or ideas.

## Who should attend

We warmly welcome participants from a broad range of domains, including: **Human health & medicine**, **Biotechnology & biomanufacturing**, **Agriculture & food**, **Environment & sustainability**, **Fundamental life sciences**, and **Life science technologies & infrastructure**.

You do **not need to be an LLM expert**. The hackathon is intended both for people who want to experiment with LLMs and for those who already have experience and want to apply that expertise to concrete research challenges.

Possible use cases include:

* **Software interoperability**: use LLMs to help different software tools interoperate through data.
* **LLMs as research assistants**: use LLM-based tools to support data analysis, coding, visualization.
* **Data discovery and access**: explore how LLMs can assist with automated data discovery and access.
* **Structured data extraction**: use LLMs to extract structured information from unstructured sources.
* **Learning and exploration**: learn about using LLMs in research and data management more generally.

## Bring your own

Participants are encouraged to bring something of their own to the hackathon. This could be:

* **Your own data** — a dataset, metadata, documentation or other resource you would like to explore with LLMs.
* **Your own software** — a research tool, workflow or API that you would like to make more interoperable or easier to use with LLMs.
* **Your own expertise** — knowledge, skills, or experience that you can contribute to a group. This might be expertise in a research domain, data management, software development, AI/LLMs, metadata, research infrastructure, or a specific scientific workflow. You do not need to arrive with a ready-made project; your expertise itself can be a valuable contribution to another participant's challenge.

The goal is to bring these together and explore a shared challenge resulting in practical experiments, prototypes, insights, or ideas for follow-up work.

The day features a combination of presentations, pitches, and collaborative hacking:

| Time  | Activity                                                                                                                                 |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 09:30 | Walk in & coffee                                                                                                                         |

| 17:00 | Closing                                                                                                                                  |
